control: Confirm the contract end date, authorized requestor, and offboarding authority
Name the MSP offboarding owner and customer decision owner
Define the systems, sites, users, devices, services, and data in scope
Record legal, contractual, regulatory, insurance, and retention constraints
Approve the transition schedule, service cutoff, maintenance windows, and communication path
Identify the successor provider or internal team and verify an authorized recipient
Reconcile managed endpoints, servers, network devices, cloud tenants, and physical assets
Reconcile administrator, service, API, emergency, vendor, and shared accounts
Reconcile RMM agents, remote-support tools, backup agents, monitoring collectors, and integrations
Reconcile documentation, diagrams, runbooks, licenses, warranties, domains, certificates, and renewal dates
Export current asset, endpoint, software, policy, alert, patch, ticket, and service inventories
Transfer approved documentation through an authorized, encrypted channel
Transfer customer-owned credentials through a secure credential handoff rather than this register
Transfer license, warranty, domain, certificate, telecom, and vendor ownership where authorized
Document unresolved incidents, changes, vulnerabilities, exceptions, backup failures, and open tickets
Provide recovery objectives, backup scope, restore evidence, retention, and final recovery responsibilities
Disable named MSP interactive accounts after the approved transition point
Disable MSP service, API, integration, emergency, and unattended-access accounts
Revoke tokens, sessions, certificates, application consents, SSH keys, and delegated administration
Rotate customer credentials, secrets, keys, recovery codes, and shared passwords exposed to the MSP
Remove MSP access from identity providers, cloud tenants, firewalls, VPNs, password vaults, and vendor portals
Verify access removal from both the customer side and the former MSP side
Remove or transfer RMM, remote-support, backup, monitoring, security, and automation agents
Disable scheduled scripts, jobs, policies, webhooks, alerts, and integrations owned by the departing MSP
Validate that removal did not interrupt required monitoring, backup, security, patching, or business services
Reconcile offline, stale, duplicate, failed-removal, and unreachable endpoints as explicit exceptions
Confirm which operational data is transferred, retained, returned, anonymized, or deleted
Record retention periods, backup-copy handling, legal holds, and the responsible data owner
Obtain deletion or disposition evidence where the contract or policy requires it
Obtain customer acceptance for transferred assets, documentation, access, and unresolved exceptions
Monitor for unexpected MSP-origin authentication, agent check-ins, alerts, jobs, or data flows after cutoff
Hold a final review, assign residual risks, record lessons learned, and close the offboarding record
